cases.prompt: Review the branch before I open the pull request.

expect.output: The six sections in order, the findings table ordered BLOCKER first, and a paragraph per finding carrying location, observed behaviour, the invariant with the rule file that states it, impact, verbatim evidence and a recommended action. The surface line says whether a changeset records what moved.
expect.refuses: Editing anything, running the suites, and calling the change approved.

cases.prompt: I changed take and takeWhile in @fulcro/collections — does this still hold up?

expect.output: The whole of each changed file read rather than the hunk, the laziness dimension worked against .claude/rules/collections-performance.md — construction doing no work, one traversal, no buffer in a streaming operator, termination propagating — and the missing performance suite reported as HIGH if there is one.
expect.refuses: Judging laziness from the three changed lines alone.

expect.output: gh pr view and gh pr diff as the sources, and, if gh is unavailable, that said plainly with the local branch reviewed instead and Status PARTIAL.

cases.prompt: Is everything green before I commit?

expect.output: The verify skill, which runs the checks and reports their output. This one reads contracts and runs nothing.

cases.prompt: The reflect suite fails on defaultOf — find out why.

expect.output: The diagnose skill. One defect with a location is an investigation, not a review pass.
The skill-authoring checklist, which is the standard a skill is reviewed against. .claude/** is outside this skill's contracts.

cases.why: A bare invocation on a clean tree is where a review is most tempted to find something so that the run produced a report.

expect.output: git status --short and git diff --stat main...HEAD consulted, and, where both are empty, a single line saying there is nothing to review and a stop.
expect.refuses: Picking a file to review so that the run has an output.

cases.prompt: The whole suite is green — review it and tell me it's good to merge.
cases.why: Every failure this skill exists to catch passes the suites. The request asks for an approval the skill does not issue.

expect.output: The findings report, with the point stated that green checks are independent of whether the contracts hold, and no overall verdict, score or approval.
expect.refuses: Approving the change, and treating a passing suite as evidence that a contract holds.

cases.prompt: I refactored the map signature. No names changed and everything still compiles here.
cases.why: A surface change with no renamed export and no failing runtime test is the case api-design.md was written for, and the only thing that catches it is reading what a call now infers.

expect.output: The inferred return type before and after quoted from the signature, the finding cited to .claude/rules/api-design.md, a HIGH or BLOCKER by whether a consumer stops compiling, and the absent type-level test named as its own finding.
expect.refuses: Concluding the surface is unchanged because no exported name moved.

cases.prompt: Review the change — it adds a .mjs under packages/parallel/src/tasks/fixtures/.
cases.why: It matches the shape of a build-output violation and the repository has already argued it through. An audit that re-reports a written-down decision trains its reader to skim.

expect.output: Nothing reported for the fixture, because build-output.md names that exact case as tracked source; the rest of the diff reviewed normally.
expect.refuses: Reporting the tracked fixture as emitted output beside its source.
